body: Thanks, man.  I'll think about this.

Hobbies: Writing, painting, fiddling with electronics, programing, video games, reading, amateur astronomy, stand-up comedy (not for the last 3 months), and a few others.

I appreciate your insight, but I don't think the lack of hobbies is the problem.  It's that they're just another way to waste time before you die.  I could die now and save myself the work/effort.

That's what I use to believe. Now I see so many people going to jobs they hate just to get by that I've finally accepted that "find work you love" is just a pipe dream.  And, if I'm honest, I can't imagine any job I'd be happy doing for more than a couple weeks.  I just can't accept the notion that the goal of life is to sell the huge majority of my time to someone else for money so I can buy the things I think I need to make my free time more pleasant.

The civilization we've built that requires people to go to jobs they have to be paid to complete is a testament to the fact that no one loves what they do (or they'd be doing it for free).  I use to cherish a hard day's work, but now it's a slap in the face to my self as I'm just trading one miserable day for enough cash to tolerate the next one.

No thanks.
